questions.statement: Which sentence is in the past continuous?
questions.context: A tense exercise in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: They were waiting for the bus.
options.feedback: 'Were waiting' joins 'were' with the -ing form 'waiting', which is the past continuous.
'Waited' with no auxiliary is the past simple, which reports a completed action.

options.text: They are waiting for the bus.
options.feedback: 'Are waiting' is the present continuous, describing a situation happening now.

options.text: They will wait for the bus.
options.feedback: 'Will wait' is the future simple and points forward in time.

questions.explanation: The past continuous is built with 'was' or 'were' plus the -ing form, so only the sentence with that structure belongs to it.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'I ___ (walk) to school when I saw the accident.'
questions.context: A description of a morning event in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Walk' with no auxiliary is the past simple and gives no sense of an ongoing action.
'Was walking' places the walk in progress before the moment of seeing the accident.
'Was walked' is the past passive and would make the speaker the thing being walked.
'Am walking' is the present continuous and cannot describe a past morning.

questions.explanation: The walking was in progress when the accident was noticed, so the past continuous 'was walking' is required.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct time expression for the past continuous.
questions.context: A grammar table in an English class in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Every Sunday' describes a repeated habit, which belongs to the present simple.
'Right now' belongs to the present continuous, not to a past tense.
'At nine last night' is a specific past moment, which is exactly when an action can be in progress.
'Next month' points to the future and needs a future tense.

questions.explanation: Expressions that point to a moment in the past, such as 'at nine o'clock last night' or 'while', go with the past continuous.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the question: 'What ___ your brother doing when the phone rang?'
questions.context: A listening exercise in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Were' goes with plural subjects and with 'you', not with a singular brother.
'Is' is the present auxiliary and would describe an action happening now.
'Did' opens a past simple question and requires the base verb 'do'.
'Was' agrees with 'your brother' and gives the past continuous question 'What was he doing'.

questions.explanation: The subject 'your brother' is singular, so the past auxiliary is 'was', placed after the question word 'what'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative past continuous: 'She ___ (not / sleep) when I called.'
questions.context: A retelling of an evening call in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: English puts the auxiliary before 'not', so 'not was' reverses the order.
'Did not sleep' is the negative past simple, not the negative past continuous.
After 'was not' the verb must take its -ing form, so the bare 'sleep' is wrong.
'Was not sleeping' places the negation in the correct position in the past continuous.

questions.explanation: The past continuous negative places 'not' after the auxiliary 'was' and before the -ing form of the verb.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'We ___ (do) our homework when the lights went out.'
questions.context: A story told in an English class in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Was' does not agree with the plural subject 'we' in the past.
'Are doing' is the present continuous and cannot sit before 'went out'.
'Were' agrees with 'we' and 'doing' is the -ing form of 'do'.
'Were' must be followed by the -ing form, so the bare 'do' is wrong.

questions.explanation: The action in progress before the interruption is 'do our homework', so the past continuous with the plural 'were' is required.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct contraction: 'It was not raining.'
questions.context: A note about the weather in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Wasnt' without an apostrophe loses the missing letter and is misspelled.
'Was not' shortens to "wasn't", with the apostrophe standing in for the missing 'o'.
"Weren't" contracts 'were not', which does not agree with the singular 'it'.
"Didn't" contracts 'did not' and belongs to the past simple.

questions.explanation: 'Was not' contracts to "wasn't" in English, so the negative sentence becomes "It wasn't raining".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct -ing form: 'He was ___ (run) to catch the bus.'
questions.context: A short description of a morning in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Run' doubles its final 'n' before -ing, giving 'running' after 'was'.
A short vowel plus a final consonant doubles that consonant before -ing in English.
Only one 'n' is added, so 'runnning' with three n's is a misspelling.
'Ran' is the past simple of 'run' and cannot take an -ing ending.

questions.explanation: 'Run' is a one-syllable verb ending in a consonant after a short vowel, so the final 'n' doubles before -ing.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.context: A test on the past continuous in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: She cook when the guests arrived.
options.feedback: 'Cook' has no auxiliary, so the clause is not a past continuous at all.

options.text: She was cooking when the guests arrived.
options.feedback: 'Was cooking' is 'was' plus the -ing form and introduces the interrupting past action.

options.text: She was cooked when the guests arrived.
options.feedback: 'Was cooked' is the past passive, not the past continuous.

options.text: She is cooking when the guests arrived.
options.feedback: 'Is cooking' is present tense and cannot describe an action before 'arrived'.

questions.explanation: Only the sentence with 'was' or 'were' plus an -ing form is grammatically a past continuous.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the function of 'while' in 'While she was sleeping, the alarm rang'?
questions.context: A grammar explanation in an English class in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: It states a reason for the alarm ringing.
options.feedback: A reason is expressed with 'because', so 'while' does not carry that meaning.

options.text: It marks a contrast between two unrelated ideas.
options.feedback: 'While' links simultaneous actions; a contrast uses 'although' or 'but'.

options.text: It expresses a condition that must be met.
options.feedback: A condition uses 'if' or 'unless', not 'while' in this usage.

options.text: It shows that one action was in progress during another.
options.feedback: 'While' introduces the ongoing action against which the other event happened.

questions.explanation: 'While' links two past events and shows that the action in the clause after it was in progress during the action in the other clause.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: 'We ___ (visit) the museum last Sunday.'
questions.context: A student describes a weekend trip with a group from Metapan, SV.

options.feedback: The past continuous describes an action in progress in the past; the trip described here is over.
'Are visiting' is the present continuous and describes what is happening now, not last Sunday.
'Last Sunday' names a completed moment, so the past simple 'visited' is the right form.
The present perfect links a past action to the present, and 'last Sunday' normally rules it out.

questions.explanation: 'Last Sunday' is finished past time, so the verb needs the past simple form 'visited' and no auxiliary at all.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression is normally used with the past continuous?
questions.context: A grammar poster about tenses in a language school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'While' links two actions in progress at the same past moment, which is the core use of the past continuous.
'Every morning' describes a habit, and habits belong to the present simple.
'Tomorrow' points to the future, so it can never introduce a past continuous.
'Now' belongs to the present continuous; the past continuous needs a past reference point.

questions.explanation: The past continuous describes an action that was in progress at a past moment, so expressions such as 'at eight o'clock last night' or 'while' fit it.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the question: 'What ___ you doing at the party last night?'
questions.context: A teacher in Sonsonate asks about an event that has already happened.

options.feedback: 'Was' goes with singular subjects such as 'he' or 'she'; 'you' always takes 'were' in the past.
'Are' is the present form of 'be' and would place the question in the present continuous.
'Did' belongs to the past simple, which takes the base verb rather than the -ing form.
'You' takes 'were' in the past, so the question reads 'What were you doing'.

questions.explanation: The subject 'you' requires the past form of 'be', which is 'were', in front of the -ing form 'doing'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'While I ___ dinner, the phone rang.'
questions.context: A retelling of a personal anecdote in a conversation class in Santa Ana, SV.

options.feedback: 'Cook' has no auxiliary, so the clause would be the past simple and 'while' would not fit it.
'While' introduces an action in progress in the past, so 'was cooking' completes the sentence.
'Was cooked' is the past passive; the subject 'I' performs the action, so the voice is wrong.
'Am cooking' is the present continuous and cannot describe an evening that has already passed.

questions.explanation: The action in progress when the phone rang is 'cook dinner', so the clause takes 'was cooking' with 'while'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'They ___ (write) an essay when the bell rang.'
questions.context: A supervisor looks into a classroom in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'They' takes 'were', and 'write' drops its silent e before -ing to give 'writing'.
'Was' agrees with a singular subject; with 'they' the past auxiliary must be 'were'.
'Write' keeps no consonant to double, so 'writting' with three t's is a misspelling.
'Are writing' is the present continuous, which cannot sit before 'when the bell rang'.

questions.explanation: The past continuous needs 'were' for a plural subject plus the -ing form, and the spelling of 'write' becomes 'writing' by dropping the silent e.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question in the past continuous: '___ you sleeping when the storm started?'
questions.context: A weather conversation after a storm in Chalatenango, SV.

options.feedback: 'Was' agrees with singular subjects; 'you' takes 'were' in the past continuous.
'Did' would require the base verb 'sleep', not the -ing form used in the past continuous.
The question word is followed by the past auxiliary 'were', giving 'Were you sleeping'.
'Are' is present tense, so the question would describe a situation happening now.

questions.explanation: In the past continuous question the auxiliary 'were' comes directly after the question word, before the subject 'you'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative: 'He ___ (not / watch) the match last night.'
questions.context: A small-group conversation about football in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The auxiliary always comes first in English negation, so 'not was' reverses the correct order.
The past continuous negative places 'not' after 'was' and before the -ing form.
'Did' builds the negative of the past simple, which never uses the -ing form of the verb.
The bare verb 'watch' cannot follow 'was'; the present of 'be' requires the -ing form.

questions.explanation: 'Not' goes after the past auxiliary 'was', and the verb 'watch' takes the -ing form 'watching'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'What ___ you ___ (do) yesterday afternoon?'
questions.context: An interview activity in a school in San Miguel, SV.

options.feedback: 'Were' provides the past auxiliary and 'doing' the -ing form, completing the past continuous question.
'Was' does not agree with 'you', and the bare verb 'do' cannot follow an auxiliary in this tense.
'Did' is followed by the base form of the verb in the past simple, never by the -ing form.
'Are' is the present auxiliary, which would put the question in the present continuous.

questions.explanation: The past continuous question needs the auxiliary 'were' and the -ing form, so the double gap is filled by 'were' and 'doing'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past continuous correctly?
questions.context: A test on tenses handed back in a secondary school in Ahuachapan, SV.

options.text: She painted the wall when the visitors arrived.
options.feedback: 'Painted' is the past simple, so it reports the finished action rather than the action in progress.

options.text: She is painting the wall when the visitors arrived.
options.feedback: 'Is painting' is present tense and cannot describe an action happening before 'arrived'.

options.text: She was painting the wall when the visitors arrived.
options.feedback: 'Was painting' is 'was' plus the -ing form and sets up the interrupting action 'arrived'.

options.text: She paints the wall when the visitors arrive.
options.feedback: 'Paints' and 'arrive' are both present simple, describing a habit instead of a past situation.

questions.explanation: The past continuous describes an action in progress in the past, so it needs 'was' or 'were' plus an -ing form of a real verb.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'The children ___ (play) football all morning.'
questions.context: A description of a school holiday in a writing workshop in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Was' goes with a singular subject, so it does not agree with the plural 'the children'.
'Are playing' is the present continuous, which describes an action happening now.
'Played' is the past simple and gives the finished action rather than the ongoing one.
'Were' agrees with 'the children' and 'playing' is the -ing form of 'play'.

questions.explanation: With a plural subject the past auxiliary is 'were', and 'play' keeps its spelling and simply takes -ing, giving 'were playing'.
questions.subject: ingles
